findings.summary: The reworked post-write hasPendingWork under-reports pending work and can silently strand clues, breaking spec §1.3's '当且仅当板面仍有非终态 clue（open/in_flight/proposed）时再投下一条触发'. postWriteState is built by applyCasOutcomes, which only rewrites the status of cards already present in the pre-write snapshot; it never accounts for clues this tick published to the board. harvestCard publishes new clue.v2 records with status 'proposed' to hd.boardChannelId (src/harvest.ts:293-299, status from clueFromWorker at src/harvest.ts:147-153), and runWrite then CASes the harvested card in_flight→explored (src/tick-run.ts:362-375). When the harvested card was the last non-terminal card, every card in postWriteState is terminal, hasPendingWork returns false, tick.md skips the continuation put (workflows/deep-research/tick/templates/tick.md:36-44), drain reports 'drained', and the freshly published proposed clues are never explored — the exact '静默零结果 = 假装完成' outcome spec §3.2 forbids. This is a regression: the previous implementation used the pre-write snapshot, which over-approximated (the prior final review recorded it as a note precisely because convergence still held); the rework traded a benign over-approximation for a work-losing under-approximation. The needed signal is already returned in result.harvestReports[].cluesPublished (src/harvest.ts:211) but is not consumed. No test covers a harvest that both terminalizes the last non-terminal card and publishes new clues, and the real F0 run recorded in the dev-note ran with EVIDENCE_CHANNEL unset (docs/dev-notes/dev_ledr_a9_tick_trigger_01.md:81-82), i.e. with zero harvest decisions, so it could not have exercised this path either.

bin/deep-research-loop.sh carries a `#!/usr/bin/env bash` shebang but is committed with mode 100644, unlike its siblings bin/tick-entry.sh, bin/worker-launcher.sh and bin/worker-placeholder.sh (all 100755), so it can only be started via an explicit `bash bin/deep-research-loop.sh`. This predates the package and no spec criterion requires it, but it sits oddly with A9's stated purpose of making the driver actually runnable, and the rework did chmod bin/tick-entry.sh for exactly this class of reason.
